title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted III
summary: Given an array of n strings of equal length, determine the smallest set of column indices to delete such that each string becomes lexicographically sorted.
statement: Given an array of n strings of equal length, determine the smallest set of column indices to delete such that each string becomes lexicographically sorted. Return the size of this minimal set.
constraints: Delete columns so every individual remaining row is nondecreasing left to right.
hints: Retained column indices must form a nondecreasing subsequence simultaneously in every row.
Run longest-path DP over column pairs compatible in all rows.
dp[j]=1+max(dp[i]) for i<j where every row[i]<=row[j].
Any valid retained set is such a path; deleting all other columns is optimal.
editorial: Any valid retained set is such a path; deleting all other columns is optimal.

tests.explanation: The longest jointly nondecreasing column subsequence has length two, so delete three.
A decreasing five-letter row can retain only one column, so delete four.
